root_idea.summary: The root centers on open-handed giving, generosity, and abundant outpouring.
root_idea.development: From the idea of giving freely and abundantly, the lexical branches extend to copious rain, excellence or quality, and the swift, excellent courser. These related developments remain distinct lexical uses rather than interchangeable meanings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural adjective جِيَاد is presented under the supported singular dictionary citation form جَوَادٌ.

senses.definition: Fleet, swift, and excellent as a horse; a superior courser.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrence has the plural adjective جِيَاد, used substantivally of horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become good, sound, approvable, or excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a thing, commodity, household article, work, or performance, and occasionally of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous; to give freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions include giving without being asked, giving what is appropriate to its recipient, and giving without seeking compensation; the object may be property or other possessions, including knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give up one’s life or spirit; to die or surrender one’s life in war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension comparing the surrender of life with giving away property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour forth abundantly: rain copiously, or an eye shed abundant tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the sky raining and of land or people being rained upon copiously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to become fleet or swift and excellent in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This verbal use describes excellence in a horse’s running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional construction with إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overcome someone in liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction compares two people in generosity and indicates superiority in it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thirst, especially to suffer vehement thirst; figuratively, to be at the point of death or destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive or derived construction, with the destructive sense explained figuratively as though destruction had rained upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome by longing and impelled toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of longing to meet or reach a person, including desire directed toward a woman; the usage is figurative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For drowsiness or sleepiness to overcome someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction explained as though sleep had rained upon the person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or contend with someone for superiority in liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may imply overcoming the other party in generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something good, sound, approvable, or excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used when supplying money or a garment in good or excellent condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or furnish something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction includes giving a dirham or piece of silver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slay or kill someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To say, express, or do something well or excellently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of speech, action, or work: one may speak well, act well, or perform excellently.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or acquire a horse of the fleet and excellent type called جَوَاد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a horse-possession construction, distinct from describing the horse’s running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to bear a child or children of liberal or generous disposition; of parents, to beget such a child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The generosity is a stated quality of the offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choose what is good or excellent and cultivate refinement or exactness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of work, manufacture, food, apparel, and the choice of what is best to be done; it may imply exceeding ordinary standards.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compare or contest with one another to determine whose argument, plea, allegation, or discourse is best.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal construction concerns superiority in reasoning or narration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or contend together in liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal use of the Form VI verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem or find something good, approvable, or excellent; to seek or select it as such.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of an object, a judgment, or an opinion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire, seek, or demand someone’s liberality or generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which the desired quality is another person’s generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire or seek that a horse be fleet, swift, and excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A horse-specific construction referring to the quality expressed by جَوَاد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come or happen well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An impersonal or event-related use recorded as a distinct Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Copious or abundant rain; rain that thoroughly irrigates everything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet of rain or a rain-bearing cloud and also as a quasi-plural for abundant showers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single episode of thirst or thirsting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of the thirst-related use, distinct from the quality meaning of جَوْدَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saffron.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical item recorded under this root with a specialized nominal meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous person; one who gives freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also describe one who gives appropriately and without seeking compensation; it is used for either sex.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Like a fleet and excellent horse; hence, in adverbial use, a long or rapid run, journey, or march.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Classical adverbial use derives from the horse sense and does not constitute a separate Quranic sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirst, especially vehement thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct noun with the thirst-related meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Drowsiness or slumber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun related to the notion of being overcome as if by a downpour.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good, sound, approvable, or excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to things, commodities, household goods, works, and performances; its plural includes جِيَادٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Better or best in goodness or excellence; more or most liberal; of a horse, swifter or more excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative form whose domain is determined by context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rained upon, especially by copious or abundant rain; of a field, garden, or land, well watered by rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial use describing land or cultivated ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by thirst, vehement thirst, or impending death or destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The thirst and destruction senses are figurative extensions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by longing or impelled by desire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative participial use related to the construction of being driven toward someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overcome or distressed by drowsiness or slumber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative participial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man possessing a horse of the fleet and excellent type called جَوَاد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A horse-possession noun or adjective, not a description of the man’s personal generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Present death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression in which death is characterized as immediately impending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who says, utters, expresses, or does much that is good or excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a poet and also to a workman or craftsman; the form can indicate frequent or abundant production of good speech or work.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer to the rain-related Form I entry.
Pointer to the horse-related Form I entry.
The horse sense is represented in the Quranic form; the adverbial travel and running use is classical-only.

cautions: The Quranic form is the plural adjective جِيَاد, normalized here under the singular citation form جَوَادٌ; its Quranic sense is kept separate from the Classical generosity and adverbial uses of the same headword.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Mufradat entry also discusses الجودي as a mountain name described as originally related by nisba to جود. No corresponding QAC form group is supplied, so it is not assigned as a public Quranic form.
